# Routstr provider node — instructions for an operator's agent

Goal: help an operator set up a Routstr node without exposing the bootstrap admin
password or assuming that a running API is a working provider. This file is a
standalone entry point for agents without an existing checkout. The commands,
Compose file and detailed human steps live in the checked-out repository; read
`docs/provider/quickstart.md` and `docs/provider/deployment.md` after cloning.

## Boundaries

- Ask for approval of the target host, release tag, upstream type, public domain,
  spending limit, Nostr publication and payout settings before those actions. A
  local-only trial needs no domain or funded wallet.
- The operator enters admin passwords, upstream keys, Cashu credentials and Nostr
  secrets in their own trusted terminal/dashboard. Use an SSH tunnel to administer
  a remote node. Never put secrets in chat, shell arguments, Git, captured logs or
  generated reports. A clean agent session may validate the workflow without
  seeing any credential.
- Never run bare `docker compose up`: stock `compose.yml` publishes port 8000 on
  all interfaces and starts Tor. Every Compose operation in this workflow uses
  `-f compose.node.yml`.
- Stop at a human authentication, funding or external-publication gate. Report the
  blocker, not a fabricated success.

## Default flow (public mode)

The default assumes the operator already has a subdomain with HTTPS and a reverse
proxy forwarding to `127.0.0.1:8000`. The node then publishes its Nostr listing on
first boot. If there is no public URL yet, use private mode and publish later.

### Phase 0 — Host

Confirm Docker with the Compose plugin, Python 3, available disk and durable
storage. Ask the operator to select a reviewed release tag; for testing the
current development branch, explicitly label it as unreviewed. Clone
`https://github.com/Routstr/routstr-core.git`, check out that ref, and inspect the
quickstart and deployment guide before running commands. Reuse an existing
checkout and state; do not overwrite `.env` or recreate a wallet.

For public mode, verify **before** starting that DNS, TLS and a reverse proxy
forward `https://<domain>` to `127.0.0.1:8000`. If any of that is missing, prefer
private mode. The dashboard is protected by the node's own admin password
(scrypt-hashed); restricting `/admin` at the proxy (IP allowlist or basic auth) is
an optional extra layer, not a setup requirement. What matters is that the
operator reads the one-time bootstrap password and rotates it.

### Phase 1 — Start

Check that the loopback port is free, then run (public):

```bash
python3 scripts/node_setup.py start --public-url https://node.example --ln-address user@wallet.example
```

or private (nothing published):

```bash
python3 scripts/node_setup.py start --private
```

If another service owns port 8000, keep it untouched and pass `--port 18080`; use
that port for `check`, the dashboard URL, the reverse proxy and later
`ROUTSTR_NODE_PORT=18080 docker compose -f compose.node.yml …` commands.

`start` prepares `.env` (never clobbering existing values), starts
`compose.node.yml` (loopback only, no Tor, analytics off on first boot), waits for the local
`/v1/info` and `/v1/models`, generates the master key and Nostr identity, and — in
public mode — publishes the listing. It also mints a long-lived CLI token and
writes it to `~/.routstr/config.json` (0600) for the Routstr CLI; skip that with
`--no-cli-token`. If that file already points at another node, `start` leaves it
alone and creates no token (see the Routstr CLI section below). A running API with zero models is **not configured**.

### Phase 2 — Back up (operator, before configuring)

The master key and identity exist as soon as the node boots. Have the operator
copy `routstr_secret.key`, `keys.db` (with any `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars), `.wallet/`
(created on first ecash activity, so absent on a fresh node) and `.env` into an encrypted off-host backup, with a tested isolated restore. The
master key decrypts the `nsec` stored in `keys.db`; keep them together:

```bash
docker compose -f compose.node.yml exec routstr /.venv/bin/python scripts/reveal_nsec.py
```

Do not ingest the revealed `nsec` or any logs into the agent context.

### Phase 3 — Dashboard (operator)

Hand the operator the dashboard address (`https://node.example/admin` in public
mode, or `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin` over an SSH tunnel). Have them read the
generated password privately from
`docker compose -f compose.node.yml logs routstr`, log in, and immediately rotate
it in Settings → Admin Settings. Then add the upstream in Providers, enable at
least one routable model, and review pricing, payout address, mints and relays.

### Phase 4 — Verify and accept

```bash
python3 scripts/node_setup.py check --public-url https://node.example
```

Require exit code 0 and a nonzero public model count (exit code 2 means the API is
running but not configured). If it fails, diagnose without printing provider
records or secrets. This proves discovery only — it is **not** a paid-inference
test.

With explicit approval of model, mint, prompt and spending limit, have the
operator run small paid non-streaming and streaming inference tests with a funded
client credential (not an admin token). Verify completion, accounting, upstream
serving, refund status and payout separately. Do not claim production acceptance
without these checks.

## Routstr CLI

The setup writes a long-lived admin token to `~/.routstr/config.json` (0600), so
the [Routstr CLI](https://github.com/routstr/routstr-cli) is ready to operate the
node. If that file already pointed at another node, `start` left it alone and
minted no token. The CLI only reads `$HOME/.routstr/config.json`, so re-run `start`
with `--cli-config /some/dir/.routstr/config.json` and run the CLI as
`HOME=/some/dir routstr …`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/routstr/routstr-cli.git
cd routstr-cli && bun install

routstr instruct          # canonical agent guide for this node
routstr schema            # full command tree as JSON
routstr status
routstr providers list
routstr providers add openrouter --api-key <key> --base-url https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

The token is **full node admin**. Give each agent its own named, expiring token
and revoke it when done (**Settings → CLI Tokens**, or
`DELETE /admin/api/cli-tokens/{id}`). On a different machine, configure the CLI
with `routstr init --node-url <url> --token <token>`. Mint another token with
`docker compose -f compose.node.yml exec routstr /.venv/bin/python scripts/create_cli_token.py --name agent`.
Never paste the token, or the generated admin password, into a chat.

## Private mode (no public URL yet)

Everything above holds, except `HTTP_URL` is unset: the node is loopback-only and
publishes nothing. Administer it over an SSH tunnel, and promote it later by
setting the public **HTTP URL** in the dashboard (the listing is then published
automatically). Approve publication with the operator before doing so.

## Handoff

Report ref/version, private/public reachability, whether password rotation was
confirmed (never the password), model count, backup/restore and paid-inference
verification status, and remaining blockers. "Local API ready" and "production
accepted" are separate outcomes. Never paste raw Docker logs or admin responses.
